entries.title: Numbers 18:1
segments:
Thou and thy sons and thy father's house; this includes the Levites with the priests; for by his father's house are meant the sons of Levi. 
 
  Bear the iniquity of the sanctuary; of all the service pertaining to the sanctuary.  It was now shown that Aaron and his sons were confirmed in the honors of the priesthood, and the Lord informed him that they must bear its responsibilities.  If any thing should be done wrong, they would be accountable. 
 
  Thou and thy sons; this includes only the priests.

entries.title: Numbers 18:3
segments: The ministry is a great and responsible work.  To be intrusted with it is a peculiar honor; and to be made faithful in discharging its duties is an unspeakable blessing.

entries.title: Numbers 18:4
segments: A stranger; one not of the tribe of Levi.

entries.title: Numbers 18:5
segments: Keep the charge of the sanctuary; to see that every thing with regard to the worship of God was done according to his direction.

entries.title: Numbers 18:6
segments: Do the service; the less sacred and more laborious parts of it.

entries.title: Numbers 18:7
segments: The stranger; one not of the family of Aaron.

entries.title: Numbers 18:8
segments: The charge of my heave-offerings; the heave-offerings and wave-offerings were presented under the priest's direction, and then, as a general rule, went to his maintenance.  Compare

entries.title: Numbers 18:9
segments:
Reserved from the fire; from such offerings as were partly burnt upon the altar. 
 
  Meat-offering--sin-offering--trespass-offering; the meat-offerings were the unbloody oblations of flour, cakes, etc.  After a portion of these had been burned on the altar, the rest fell to the priest.  The same was the law in respect to sin-offerings and trespass-offerings. But the peace-offerings belonged to the offerer, with the exception of the wave-breast and heave-shoulder.  Thus a provision was made for the support of the priests and their families.  See

entries.title: Numbers 18:12
segments: The best of the oil--the best of the wine; the reference here is to the first-fruits of the wine and oil, of which it was the duty of the Israelites to give a portion to the priest, and which were to be of the best quality.

entries.title: Numbers 18:14
segments: Devoted; solemnly given to God.  Provided it was any thing that might be eaten or otherwise consumed, it went to the priest.  But vessels of gold, silver, or brass, went to the service of the sanctuary.

entries.title: Numbers 18:15
segments: Shalt thou redeem; this was done by the priest's receiving a specified sum of money in exchange for it.

entries.title: Numbers 18:16
segments: That are to be redeemed; that is, of men.  The first-born of unclean beasts were to be redeemed by a lamb.
According to thine estimation; that is, according to the valuation prescribed to thee in the law; for this was not left wholly to the priest's discretion.

entries.title: Numbers 18:19
segments:
A covenant of salt; a perpetual, permanent covenant. 
 
While ministers of religion are precluded by their office from engaging in worldly business, and thus obtaining a support for themselves and their families, it is the will of God that they should be supported by those for whose spiritual good they minister.

entries.title: Numbers 18:21
segments: The tenth; a tenth part of the produce or increase of the property of the other tribes.

entries.title: Numbers 18:23
segments: They shall bear their iniquity; if any thing is done wrong, they shall bear the blame.

entries.title: Numbers 18:27
segments: As though it were the corn of the threshing-floor; that is, it shall be given by you to the high-priest just as common Israelites give a tithe from the corn of their threshing-floor to the common priests.

entries.title: Numbers 18:32
segments:
Ye shall bear no sin; they would not do wrong in eating, as they would if they should not first offer a tenth for the use of the priests according to the Lord's directions. 
 
God requires not only that his ministers and their families should be supported, but also that they should have something for pious and charitable uses; and in devoting all to him, they may gratefully partake of what they need, and expect his blessing to rest upon them.
